attacks.claim: Downgrade silently loses user data. v1 keeps only 4 of 8 periods, and a 4.7 schedule edit makes the cloud discard the v2 copy, so periods 5-8 are gone on re-upgrade. The user gets no notice and no path back to the full schedule. The 'simplified' warning is conditional and is not specified for the downgrade-then-re-upgrade path.
attacks.evidence: "When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy, so a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule." / "The app shows 'Some schedule changes were simplified' if v2 had more than 4 periods."

attacks.claim: The v1 projection that downgrade safety depends on is underspecified. It has no tie-break or validity rule for overlapping or out-of-order periods, and QA exercised one schedule per hardware rev rather than arbitrary 8-period inputs. The downgrade-then-re-upgrade combination with a 4.7 edit in between is also not tested.
attacks.evidence: "keeping the 4 periods closest to the user's wake / leave / return / sleep anchors" / "v1/v2 schedule: edit on 4.8, downgrade to 4.7 via OTA, schedule present and correct | Pass (rev B/C/D)"

attacks.claim: HVAC fault telemetry is a stage-advance criterion but not a paging trigger, and schedule-sync errors and HVAC fault codes have no alert at all. A spike in HVAC faults during a 3-4 day stage would not reach on-call until the stage gate is reviewed.
attacks.evidence: "Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1% of updated units in any 6 h window or offline rate rises 0.5 points over baseline." / "HVAC fault telemetry not above 4.7 baseline"

attacks.claim: Away Assist's logic (no motion for 2 h during home periods triggers Away) has only happy-path tests. Stationary occupants (sleeping, sitting still) and pets are not covered, so a sensor false negative could set Away and cool an occupied home for opted-in users. Monitoring also has no Away-accuracy or occupancy-complaint signal.
attacks.evidence: "Away Assist: off after upgrade by default; on → Away after 2 h no motion, back on motion; off → history deleted | Pass" / "Monitoring" section lists only boot reverts, self-test failures, offline rate, HVAC fault codes, schedule-sync errors.

attacks.claim: The boot-revert metric may undercount units that fail in a way that prevents self-test reporting, and the fleet-wide 0.5-point offline threshold can hide a regional or hardware-rev cluster even though the rollout is stratified.
attacks.evidence: "If 4.8 fails to boot or fails its post-boot self-test 3 times, the unit reverts to 4.7 automatically." / "offline rate rises 0.5 points over baseline"

attacks.claim: The artifact does not say whether Home/Away state writes from devices to the cloud are authenticated or integrity-protected. A spoofed or replayed write could alter what the app displays.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: authentication and integrity controls for Home/Away state events. "Only the resulting Home/Away state is sent to the cloud (needed to show it in the app)"

attacks.claim: The privacy conclusion ('does not change existing data sharing') rests on legal review whose content is not in the artifact. There is no stated jurisdictional analysis for Canadian units (e.g., Quebec Law 25) covering inferred occupancy data.
attacks.evidence: "Privacy notice section 3 updated (legal review LGL-4471)." / ABSENT: Canadian/Quebec privacy analysis for occupancy inference.

attacks.claim: The energy headline reports a heating-runtime reduction, not a savings figure, and omits that the feature is off by default. The trial design (controls, selection) is only linked, not stated, so a typical user may overestimate the benefit.
attacks.evidence: "In our 2025-26 field trial of 412 homes, Away Assist cut heating runtime by a median of 6%."

attacks.claim: Install deferral is tested only at the 5 °C low bound. The 32 °C upper bound is untested, and there is no escalation if the indoor sensor is faulty and reads out of range persistently, which could defer updates indefinitely.
attacks.evidence: "Temperature deferral at 5 °C chamber test | Pass, install deferred" / "Install is deferred if indoor temperature is below 7 °C or above 32 °C"

attacks.claim: The +0.4% telemetry projection assumes one event per state change, with no bound on flapping near the 2 h threshold. The egress estimate also omits retries and re-pulls, so both figures are floors rather than budgets.
attacks.evidence: "Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change; projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest." / "OTA egress: 2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB"

attacks.claim: Accessibility and French verification covers only app 9.3 screens. On-device thermostat strings and any on-device Away indicator are not shown to be tested.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: on-device UI and string verification. "App 9.3 new strings in English and French (Canada) | Pass"
